title: Rapid Shallow Breathing Index (RSBI)
keywords: measured during a T-piece or low PS trial
purpose: The most-used bedside predictor of weaning success — the ratio of respiratory rate to tidal volume during a brief period of spontaneous breathing (T-piece or PS 0–5 / PEEP 0–5). One data point that supports, but does not replace, a passed spontaneous breathing trial.

interpretation.label: < 105 — favourable; supports proceeding to a spontaneous breathing trial / extubation if the other criteria are met
≥ 105 — substantially higher weaning-failure risk. Reassess the cause of respiratory failure, sedation, secretions, fluid balance, and cardiac function before another attempt

notes: Measure after ~1 min of spontaneous breathing on minimal support. Integrate with: a passed SBT (the primary test), secretion burden, cough strength, cuff-leak, mental status, and overall trajectory. RSBI performs less well in women, small patients, and with a small ETT (resistance inflates the rate).
buildNote: Formula engine — Vt is entered in mL and divided by 1000 for the L in the denominator.
